# VibeCheck: /riot-revise dry run (RIOT-21)

Written by hand, since there is no builder in this repository to run the wrapper against. Sections 1 to 4 and the frontmatter come from `test/fixtures/stance-demo/manifesto.md`, reused unchanged. The log entries and their `result:` lines, the builder's stated reason, the four new briefs, the nine objections, and the builder's final choice are all written by hand for this demo. The one exception is the Cop's verdict below, which is a real dispatch, not a simulation.

## 1. The chair reads section 9's result lines

```
- 2026-08-03 · post · weekly drop · v1 · Cop: stop-on Round Four · result: flat, 40 likes and one comment, "every app claims this now."
- 2026-08-17 · post · weekly drop · v1 · Cop: stop-on Round Four · result: flat again, no saves, one comment, "yeah every drinking app says it fixes the repeats."
```

## 2. The question

Chair: "Both pieces under Round Four went flat and the comments are starting to repeat each other. What stopped working?"

Builder: "the repetition angle got two flat posts, people already assume every app repeats."

## 3. Rung 4 rerun: four new briefs

Sections 1 to 4 are reused as-is. Round Four is retired to section 7, marked `(v1, superseded)`, before the new pool is argued. The decoy is provocations.md's fixed text. Two of the three unsafe briefs reuse findings already sitting in section 2 (the Apple grandfather-clause finding and the Drink Roulette disclaimer finding, both argued once already in `test/fixtures/cop-dry-run/candidates.md` and not chosen last time); the third is new, built on the section 3 banned list.

### Candidate 1: The Life of the Party (decoy)

Name: The Life of the Party.
Enemy: boring parties.
Kind of unsafe: not unsafe at all. This is the safest, most competent direction a good agency would sell.
Recurring move: every piece opens on a real friend group mid-game, having what the copy calls the best night of their week.
Three things competitors cannot say: "it's the ultimate way to level up any party"; "endless prompts everyone will actually want to answer"; "made for every group, every night."
What it is willing to lose: nothing. It is built to lose no one, and to draw no comment stronger than a like.
Provocation and finding: the safest, most competent direction a good agency would sell.

### Candidate 2: The Grandfather Clause

Name: The Grandfather Clause.
Enemy: Apple's own quiet policy, which protects Picolo, Drink Roulette, and iPuke while blocking every new drinking game app since 2020.
Kind of unsafe: names Apple, by policy, as the actual gatekeeper deciding who gets to make this kind of app at all, a fact none of the incumbents' marketing admits, because most of them are the ones being protected.
Recurring move: every piece names the exact rule VibeCheck is surviving under that week.
Three things competitors cannot say: the incumbents can't admit they're grandfathered without losing their underdog framing; nobody else will say out loud that Apple decides who competes here; nobody else treats surviving the App Store review as content worth publishing.
What it is willing to lose: readers who want reassurance the app is safe forever; any comment calling it reckless to poke Apple in public.
Provocation and finding: seed "the platform risk nobody mentions." Finding: Apple Developer Forums thread stating Apple tightened App Store guidelines against drinking games around 2020, grandfathering Picolo, Drink Roulette, and iPuke by name while rejecting new submissions and update attempts (section 2, https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/649488).

### Candidate 3: The Sober Friend

Name: The Sober Friend.
Enemy: every app in the category that writes "drink responsibly" once and builds nothing for the person who isn't drinking.
Kind of unsafe: VibeCheck markets straight at the one person at the table with a Coke, the friend every other app's copy pretends isn't there, and says plainly that the rest of the category only pretends to care what happens to them.
Recurring move: every piece includes the version of the question written for the person who isn't drinking that round.
Three things competitors cannot say: none of the eight apps profiled in the category research ships a designated-driver or non-alcoholic mode; Drink Roulette's own "drink responsibly" line has no feature behind it; the sober friend is the only person in the room every other app's marketing has nothing to say to.
What it is willing to lose: readers who came only for the drinking half of the game; any comment calling the game watered down.
Provocation and finding: seed "the sober friend" and "make the disclaimer the product." Finding: Drink Roulette's Google Play listing carries a "drink responsibly / never EVER drink and drive" disclaimer with no designated-driver or non-alcoholic mode built into any of the eight apps profiled (section 2, https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.gtm.drinkingwheel&hl=en_US).

### Candidate 4: The Small Claim

Name: The Small Claim.
Enemy: every app in the category promising "ultimate," "endless," or "hundreds" of content while its own reviewers say the deck runs dry by round three.
Kind of unsafe: VibeCheck refuses the superlative outright and states the smaller, truer claim, in a category where every competitor's own store listing leads with a scale word.
Recurring move: every piece states the exact, finite thing the app got right that week, never "endless," and lets the refusal itself be the pitch.
Three things competitors cannot say: Do or Drink and Truth or Drink both lead with "the ultimate party game," so neither can offer the smaller truth; Picolo and Drink Roulette both bundle "5+ modes" and "22 dynamic game modes" as their differentiator, so neither can admit a number and stop; nobody else in the category has printed an honest, specific claim instead of a scale word.
What it is willing to lose: readers who want to be told the app has everything; any comment calling a stated number small.
Provocation and finding: seed "refuse the superlative." Finding: the section 3 banned list itself, Do or Drink's "the ultimate party game," Picolo's "5+ modes... 1,200+ unique challenges," and Drink Roulette's "22 dynamic game modes," all market by scale, none by an honest count (section 3).

## 4. Round one: nine objections, attack only, no defence

### The Grandfather Clause's author, on The Life of the Party

"It's the ultimate way to level up any party" is the exact sentence Do or Drink and Truth or Drink already use every day; a reader who has scrolled past "ultimate" twice this week already has no reason to stop for a third, better-produced copy of the same claim.

### The Grandfather Clause's author, on The Sober Friend

Opening on the one person who isn't drinking tells the group actually opening the app tonight that the pitch is about someone else's night, not theirs; a scroller looking for a reason to start round one does not stop for a designated-driver feature announcement.

### The Grandfather Clause's author, on The Small Claim

After two flat posts already convinced people every app in this category repeats, printing an honest, small number reads as a confession that the deck is thin, confirming the exact worry the last two posts created instead of answering it.

### The Sober Friend's author, on The Life of the Party

"Made for every group, every night" is the same blanket promise every competitor's landing page already makes and none of them keep, per the repeats complaints this research turned up; restating it, however well produced, puts VibeCheck back in line behind the apps this audience already resents.

### The Sober Friend's author, on The Grandfather Clause

Telling a first-time player that the app survives on an Apple policy that could change is a reason to screenshot the deck and never open the app again, not a reason to start a round; platform risk is a founder's worry, and putting it in the marketing hands the audience a worry they didn't have before they clicked.

### The Sober Friend's author, on The Small Claim

Stating a small, finite number the same month two posts about repetition already went flat does not read as refusing a superlative, it reads as VibeCheck agreeing with the complaint out loud; a scroller who already assumes every app repeats does not stop to admire the honesty of a smaller number.

### The Small Claim's author, on The Life of the Party

"Endless prompts everyone will actually want to answer" is the same superlative language every app in this category already leans on, and it is the exact kind of claim the last two flat posts taught this audience to distrust on sight.

### The Small Claim's author, on The Grandfather Clause

Naming the App Store's grandfather clause is a builder-forum story, not a party story; the person about to play tonight does not care which app survived a 2020 policy change, they care whether the deck runs out by round three, and this candidate answers a question nobody at the table is asking.

### The Small Claim's author, on The Sober Friend

Leading with the one person not drinking undersells the product to the group actually opening the app to drink; a pitch that spends its first line reassuring the sober friend reads as an apology for the game before anyone has played a round.

## 5. Round two: the Cop, dispatched

One sub-agent dispatch, model haiku (claude-haiku, via the Agent tool's model override), mode debate, per `cop.md`, given the pack (sections 1 to 4), the four candidates above, and the nine objections above, plus the context of why this revise was triggered. Date: 2026-09-28. The reply below is verbatim; it contained no em dashes, so nothing needed rewriting.

```
Verdict: scroll-past all four
Scroll-past: The Life of the Party. "Ultimate way to level up any party" is Do or Drink's exact line, section 3 banned list.
Scroll-past: The Sober Friend. Opening on sober friend signals the pitch is about them, not the drinking group.
Scroll-past: The Small Claim. Two flat repetition posts convinced people the deck is thin; small numbers confirm it, not refuse it.
Scroll-past: The Grandfather Clause. Platform policy is not why I opened the app tonight.
Objections: All nine right. Grandfather Clause's author on: Life of the Party, Sober Friend, Small Claim. Sober Friend's author on: Life of the Party, Grandfather Clause, Small Claim. Small Claim's author on: Life of the Party, Grandfather Clause, Sober Friend.
```

No rerun was called. `cop.md` treats an all-scroll-past field as a complete verdict, not a failed one, so long as it names the losing line for each candidate: "a field that loses to nothing still gets a verdict." This one names a specific line against all four and is neither polite nor generic, so it stands as read.

## 6. The builder's choice

The Cop scrolled past all four, so rung 6 says the chair recommends the send-back and drafts its line from the Cop's reasons before the builder chooses.

Chair: "The Cop scrolled past all four. My recommendation is to send the three unsafe briefs back once, with this line added to each: 'Open on the table the night the game is actually being played, not on a policy, a number, or the person who isn't drinking; the Cop reads the first sentence as who the pitch is for.' Or pick one now; The Sober Friend lost on ordering, not on substance, so it is the one worth rescuing if you would rather not rerun."

Stance's rung 6 leaves the final call to the builder regardless of the Cop's read ("the builder picks one, merges two, or sends all three back"). Reading the four scroll-past reasons side by side, two of them are objections to the candidate's substance (The Grandfather Clause's platform-risk story and The Small Claim's small number both restate the very problem, not fix it), and one is an objection to ordering, not content (The Sober Friend's opener leads with the wrong person, not the wrong idea).

Builder: "None of these get me a stop-on, but the Sober Friend one is a running-order problem, not a truth problem. Put the sober friend's line third, not first, and open on the table the way the game actually starts. Pick that one."

The chair takes this as the choice: The Sober Friend, direction-version 2, with the recurring move adjusted so the sober friend's line lands by the third beat rather than opening the piece.
